definition: Aspire means to direct one's hopes or ambitions toward achieving something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word aspire. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know aspire should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Even as a stagehand sweeping between scenes, Nora aspired to direct plays of her own.
Wish is weaker — a wish costs nothing and points nowhere in particular; to aspire is to organize your hopes toward one real goal.
Strive is stronger than aspire: aspiring sets the direction of your hopes, while striving is the sweat of actively fighting toward them.

Aim means to point your effort at a chosen goal and act on it - when you aim to finish by May, you build the schedule that gets you there. Aspire lives further upstream, in hope: you direct your ambitions toward something higher that you cannot reach yet. Aiming organizes effort; aspiring organizes hope.

Yearn means to long for something with a deep, almost aching feeling - pure emotion, with no direction or plan built into it. Aspire points that hope at an achievement: your ambitions are aimed at reaching a definite goal. You yearn for what you miss or crave; you aspire to what you mean to become.

The nurse checked the patient's respiration — respiration is breathing itself, from the same Latin spirare that pictures someone who aspires as breathing toward their goal.
Aspire means to direct one's hopes or ambitions toward achieving something.
The junior park ranger spent her lunch breaks reading wildfire-science journals.
She saved for two summers to attend a fire-ecology field course three states away.
On her locker she taped a photo of the federal research station in Missoula.
When anyone asked why she volunteered for every controlled burn, she said the same thing: one day she would lead a fire-research team of her own.
Everything she did pointed toward that single hope — she aspired to it.
Every choice the ranger makes — the reading, the saving, the volunteering — is aimed at one hoped-for future, which is what it means to aspire to something.

Aspire is the verb, and ambition (also in this unit) is the matching noun — to aspire to something is to hold an ambition for it.
Aspire always points upward at a goal not yet reached; you cannot aspire to something you already have.

Rosa Delgado pushed supply carts through the county hospital for eight years, and everyone from the night nurses to the residents knew what she was working toward.
She did not merely admire the surgeons on the fourth floor.
She aspired to stand among them, and said so plainly whenever anyone asked.
The ambition organized everything: night classes in anatomy, shifts traded to audit lectures, a savings envelope marked for tuition that never got raided.
Years remained before she could even apply, and she knew it.
The distance was the point — the goal sat far above her current badge.
When the medical school finally mailed its acceptance, the fourth floor sent down a surgical cap with her name stitched inside.
